audit: Checked once: after the research, agents that had not written the records compared all 78 cases with the saved source texts (no new searches) and raised 122 findings, of which 22 were plain errors. 101 were applied; 21 were rejected: source-grade upgrades against the grading rule above, and a suggestion to cite a copy that was not obtained within the source-fetching rules. The corrected text was not audited again, long reports were read in the relevant parts only, and the audit cannot catch an error in a source.

cases.name: Halifax Explosion
cases.substance: picric acid, TNT, gun cotton and benzol cargo
cases.deaths_note: Counts differ: Canadian Encyclopedia says nearly 2,000 died, gives 1,631 dead or missing in 1918 morgue records and a revised figure of 1,946 by 2004 (used here). Maritime Museum of the Atlantic says more than 1,700. A Northern Mariner article says two thousand, and quotes a 1962 newspaper figure of at least 1,600. No official final figure was read.
cases.what_happened: The inbound French munitions ship Mont-Blanc and the outbound Norwegian Imo collided in the harbour Narrows. Fire broke out aboard Mont-Blanc, which drifted to the Halifax shore and exploded about 20 minutes later, devastating the Richmond district.
causes: Collision after conflicting manoeuvres and signals in the Narrows; sparks started a fire
Sources differ on what first ignited: benzol on deck (journal article) or dry picric acid below deck (encyclopedia)
Fault: the 1918 inquiry blamed Mont-Blanc; a split Supreme Court of Canada decision and then the Privy Council (1920) found both ships at fault

The journal author describes confused wartime control of harbour traffic and earlier warnings that officials did not act on, and argues that blame was focused on the pilot, which drew attention away from federal failings

learnings.text: Movements of explosive cargo through populated harbours need positive traffic control and clear right-of-way.
People who know a cargo is explosive need a fast way to warn the shore; spectators gathered to watch the fire.
The first official finding of fault may be overturned; read the appeals as well as the inquiry.

questions: What separation, routing and timing rules would you set for a munitions or ammonium nitrate ship passing a city?
How would you tell harbourside residents in minutes that a burning ship may explode?

cases.name: Oppau fertiliser silo explosion
cases.deaths_note: A BASF author's review gives 507 killed and 1,917 injured and notes that figures differ by source. BASF's history page says over 500 dead and about 2,000 hurt.
cases.what_happened: Blasting, used routinely to loosen caked fertiliser in a silo holding about 4,500 t of ammonium sulfate nitrate, set off a detonation. About 20,000 earlier blasting operations had passed without notable incident. The works and surrounding town were devastated.
causes: Reichstag committee: causes could not be reliably determined (as quoted by BASF)
Later review: a new spray-drying process changed physical properties and made the salt easier to detonate
Later review: a fine fraction richer in ammonium nitrate probably built up unnoticed and was initiated by loosening charges; definite proof is not possible

learnings.text: Assess a process change before it is made, including its effect on the hazard properties of the material, and update the safety concept.
Where the hazard potential is extreme, no single deviation should be able to release it.
A long incident-free record under old conditions is not evidence of safety after the product or process changes.

questions: Which material properties would your change procedure require to be re-tested after a change of drying method?
What routine practice on your site is justified mainly by the number of times it has not gone wrong?

cases.name: East Ohio Gas LNG tank failure and fire
cases.deaths_note: Encyclopedia of Cleveland History says the toll reached 130. No official count was read.
cases.what_happened: A liquefied natural gas storage tank (No. 4) failed and its contents ignited. About 20 minutes later a sphere also failed. Liquid and vapour flowed along streets into sewers, where vapour exploded, and fire swept homes and businesses near the plant.
causes: Bureau of Mines (as summarised in an NFPA staff presentation): a definitive cause could not be determined
Contributing factors listed: wooden support of the inner tank, steel prone to brittle failure, and a flaw in tank or welding
Spilled LNG entered sewers and vapour mixed with air
No evidence found of operating error or sabotage

learnings.text: Separate LNG facilities widely from inhabited areas and take great care to keep spills out of storm sewers.
Provide dikes, and establish low-temperature properties of metals before using them for cryogenic storage.
A crack at first cool-down should prompt a documented re-examination of whether the material and design are suitable, in addition to repair and changes to cool-down practice.

questions: How do you size and locate impoundment so a total tank failure cannot reach drains or neighbours?
What material tests and acceptance evidence would you demand for a cryogenic containment steel today?

cases.name: Texas City ammonium nitrate ship explosions
cases.deaths_note: The report as of 29 April 1947 records 433 bodies recovered and about 135 missing. It is an interim count, so no single integer is given.
cases.what_happened: Fire was found in bagged fertiliser-grade ammonium nitrate in a hold of the Grandcamp at the dock. Someone ordered no water, to protect the cargo, though hose lines were later in use. The ship exploded about an hour after discovery; a second ammonium nitrate ship, High Flyer, exploded the next night. Docks and a nearby chemical plant were destroyed.
causes: The report says the fire's time of origin and cause will probably never be known
It judges that plentiful water early on would probably have extinguished it; steam use was reported but unconfirmed
Hazards of ammonium nitrate were little known to handlers; bags carried no hazard warning
Ammonium nitrate packed in combustible bags let the fire spread very rapidly once established

learnings.text: Label containers clearly as hazardous and instruct everyone who handles the material.
Fight ammonium nitrate fires with large quantities of water and respiratory protection; do not rely on steam.
Ports should tell the fire chief in advance about hazardous cargo and hold a worst-case disaster plan.
Prohibit smoking and open lights, and segregate ammonium nitrate from combustibles.

questions: Who in a modern port must know where ammonium nitrate is, and how quickly can they find out?
How would you write a stop-or-fight decision for a fire involving an oxidiser cargo near a city?

cases.name: Feyzin refinery propane sphere BLEVE
cases.deaths_note: HSE and IChemE LPB 251 both give 18 dead; injured is 81 (HSE) or 84 (LPB 251).
cases.what_happened: While water was being drained from the bottom of a propane sphere, a blockage cleared and propane escaped through valves that could no longer be closed. The cloud ignited, probably at a car about 160 m away. Fire engulfed the sphere, which ruptured while crews cooled neighbouring vessels, and further vessel failures followed.
causes: Drain valves opened in an order contrary to a recently issued procedure; a probable ice or hydrate plug then cleared and the valves froze open
Poorly designed manual drain with difficult valve access and discharge directly beneath the valves
Escaping liquid accumulated under the sphere instead of draining away
Fire-fighting approach left the engulfed sphere without cooling

learnings.text: Avoid direct draining of LPG vessels; use a closed system or an isolatable de-watering pot, with a remotely operated isolation valve on the drain.
Protect spheres with deluge water, fire-resistant insulation or mounding and protected legs, and slope the ground so spills run away from the vessels.

Train responders for fire-engulfed vessels: cool the affected tank and nearby installations while keeping people and vehicles as far away as possible. Time to BLEVE is hard to judge, and the bulletin notes that the cautious philosophy is to evacuate and shelter rather than try to extinguish.

questions: Which of your drain or sample points could release pressurised liquid that one operator cannot stop, and how would you redesign it?
What information would an incident commander need to decide between cooling a vessel and withdrawing?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: HSE states that design measures such as insulation or permanent water sprays on spheres and leg reinforcement were taken into codes of practice after the incident.

cases.name: Flixborough (Nypro UK) vapour cloud explosion
cases.what_happened: A reactor with a leaking crack was removed and a temporary bypass fitted between its neighbours so production could continue. On a Saturday afternoon the 20-inch bypass ruptured, releasing a large quantity of cyclohexane that formed a cloud and exploded. Eighteen of the dead were in the control room.
causes: Failure of the temporary bypass, installed without drawings, adequate calculations or pressure testing (HSE; IChemE paper on the Court of Inquiry)
Plant modification made without a full assessment of consequences
HSE allows that a fire on an adjacent 8-inch line might have brought about the bypass failure; an IChemE paper reports that the Inquiry considered this alternative highly improbable and dismissed it

learnings.text: Design, build, test and maintain modifications to the same standard as the original plant.
Position and design control rooms and other occupied buildings for the possibility of a sudden major event.
A temporary repair needed to keep production going deserves at least as much independent engineering review as a permanent one.

questions: Who on your site has the competence and authority to reject a temporary piping modification?
Which occupied buildings would you move or strengthen if a large flammable release occurred today?

cases.name: DSM Beek naphtha cracker explosion
cases.what_happened: During start-up of a naphtha cracker, vapour escaped from the depropaniser section and ignited, causing a large vapour cloud explosion and numerous fires. HSE records 14 dead and 107 injured, three of them off site. The alarm was not sounded before the explosion.
causes: Evidence suggested low-temperature embrittlement at the depropaniser feed drum; instrument records were destroyed
A de-ethaniser upset sent much colder, C2-rich liquid to a drum that normally ran warm
Initial fracture thought to be on a small pipe to the relief valve; it occurred at a weld which, with ageing, may fail at a higher temperature than the drum material limit

learnings.text: Set minimum design temperature from upset and start-up cases, including flashing, and apply it to welds and small-bore connections as well as shells.
Raising the alarm should not depend on a verbal instruction left for others to act on; anyone who learns of a release should sound it directly.

questions: Which upstream upsets could chill equipment on your unit below its minimum design metal temperature?
How would you test that any person who sees a release can raise the site alarm without delay?

cases.name: Seveso (ICMESA) dioxin release
cases.deaths_note: HSE states no human deaths were attributed to TCDD. Many people fell ill and thousands of animals died or were slaughtered.
cases.what_happened: A trichlorophenol batch was shut down at the end of a shift with most solvent still in the reactor, leaving it without stirring or cooling. Hours later the bursting disc ruptured and vented a cloud containing dioxin over neighbouring municipalities. Warnings to authorities and the public were badly delayed.
causes: Batch interrupted contrary to operating procedures and left unstirred and uncooled
Studies showed weaker exotherms, besides the known main one, that could lead to runaway; LPB 251 says the way the reaction started in the unstirred reactor was not understood at the time
No vessel to catch or destroy vented material, although the disc maker had recommended a second receiver

Bursting disc set pressure and purpose are reported differently: HSE gives 3.5 bar, to guard the compressed-air transfer, and says a lower setting would have vented at a less hazardous temperature; LPB 251 gives 3.8 bar, intended to protect the initial reaction stage

learnings.text: Understand reaction thermodynamics, including side reactions and decompositions under plausible procedural deviations.
Route batch reactor relief to containment wherever possible.
Prepare and exercise emergency plans with external responders, and give authorities timely, usable hazard information.

questions: What happens on your batch reactor if the step is abandoned halfway at the end of a shift?
What relief discharge destination would you accept for a reaction that can form a highly toxic by-product?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: IChemE LPB 251 says many of the lessons became requirements of the EU Seveso Directives.

cases.name: Los Alfaques campsite propylene tanker disaster
cases.place: Alcanar / Sant Carles de la Rapita, Tarragona
cases.deaths_note: HISTORY (grade C) gives 215 dead. ScienceDaily, summarising research on Spanish chemical accidents (grade C), gives 217. No official figure was read.
cases.what_happened: A road tanker carrying liquefied propylene came to grief beside a crowded holiday campsite on the Spanish Mediterranean coast and exploded in a very large fireball. More than 200 people died and many survivors had severe burns. According to HISTORY, the truck hit a wall, and some witnesses reported a fire before the crash.
causes: HISTORY: the truck crashed into a concrete wall for unknown reasons
HISTORY: some witnesses reported a fire on the truck before the crash
The sources read do not establish why the tank failed

learnings.text: ScienceDaily quotes a researcher saying the accident was a turning point for the safety of road transport of chemicals.
Routing of pressurised flammable cargoes should consider dense temporary populations such as campsites, not only permanent housing.

questions: Which temporary or seasonal populations lie along your dangerous-goods routes?
What tanker design and filling controls would you require before accepting a liquefied-gas load?

cases.name: Vila Soco (Cubatao) gasoline pipeline fire
cases.deaths_note: Strongly disputed. The official figure is 93. A truth commission of the Cubatao bar association believes the toll may exceed 500; the news report says the state prosecutor's office worked with scenarios of 508, 631 and more than 700, which include estimated missing children (86 bodies documented). The fire ran from the night of 24 into 25 February.
cases.what_happened: Gasoline leaked from a Petrobras pipeline running through mangrove beside a settlement built largely on stilts. The fuel spread under the homes and ignited around the night of 24 to 25 February, and fire swept the settlement.
causes: News account: later investigations pointed to a communication failure between refinery and terminal, with a receiving valve shut during a transfer, probably overpressuring the line
Poor maintenance of old pipelines also not ruled out; a commission member alleges operating error and lack of maintenance
Ignition source unknown

learnings.text: Make both ends of a transfer confirm the valve line-up before pumping starts.
Keep pipeline rights-of-way clear of housing and reassess the line's risk when settlement encroaches.
Treat a public report of a fuel leak as an emergency requiring pumps to stop.

questions: What interlock or positive confirmation would stop a transfer into a closed terminal valve?
When informal housing already sits on a pipeline route, what can the operator do in the short and long term?

cases.name: Abbeystead valve house methane explosion
cases.what_happened: Visitors were gathered in a valve house at the outfall of a water transfer scheme. Shortly after pumping began, methane that had collected during 17 days without pumping was displaced into the building and exploded. Sixteen people died and nobody in the valve house escaped injury. No ignition source was positively identified.
causes: Ignition of a methane-air mixture accumulated in the valve house
Gas displaced from a void at the end of the tunnel after 17 days without pumping
Methane hazard, including gas dissolved in inflowing water, not recognised in design or operation
Operation departed from the designers' manual; procedures changed without proper consultation

learnings.text: HSE states that a discharge system open to atmosphere would have prevented the explosion.
Consult properly on the effect of operating-procedure changes and make sure operators understand special design features.
Screen utility and water assets for flammable gas hazards, not only plants that handle hydrocarbons on purpose.

questions: Where in a nominally non-hazardous system could gas collect during a long idle period?
How should designers communicate an operating step that is safety critical for a reason operators cannot see?

cases.name: San Juan Ixhuatepec LPG terminal disaster
cases.place: San Juan Ixhuatepec, Mexico City area
cases.deaths_note: IChemE summary gives 542 as the official toll and says unofficial estimates were higher (shanty town population unknown). The HSE case study says about 500.
cases.what_happened: An LPG transfer line ruptured at a state-owned storage terminal during filling. The escaping cloud drifted to a flare and ignited. About 15 minutes after the release began, the first of a series of BLEVEs occurred over roughly an hour and a half, destroying the terminal and hitting nearby housing.
causes: Loss of containment from an 8-inch LPG line; IChemE says overpressure or overfilling, exact cause unknown because evidence was destroyed
No gas detection; emergency isolation operated late
Close vessel spacing and bund walls that let LPG pool around vessels
Firewater system disabled by the initial blast
Housing had grown close to the terminal fence

learnings.text: Provide remotely operated emergency isolation valves on bulk LPG vessels, closing slowly enough to avoid pressure surge.
Enforce land-use rules that keep minimum separation between major hazard sites and homes.
Study escalation when setting layout, spacing and fire protection.

questions: How would you grade and drain the ground under pressurised LPG vessels so that a leak cannot feed fire under them?
What should operators do on an unexplained pressure drop in a filling line before the source is found?

cases.name: Bhopal methyl isocyanate release
cases.deaths_note: ARIA gives 3,787 (2,259 immediate) as official Madhya Pradesh figures, and 5,000-25,000 across other sources; it says the true number will never be known. A PTI report in Deccan Herald quotes a state official that compensation was paid for 5,295 deaths; an NGO there claims over 25,000.
cases.what_happened: During the night of 2-3 December, water entered a methyl isocyanate storage tank. A runaway reaction lifted the relief system. The scrubber was overwhelmed and the flare was out of service, so a dense toxic cloud drifted into settlements beside the plant. The public siren sounded after most of the release had occurred.
causes: About 500 L of water entered a tank holding 42 t of MIC; how it got in (washing error, connection error or sabotage) is contested
Refrigeration and nitrogen pressurisation of the tank were out of service
Scrubber ineffective and undersized; flare dismantled for maintenance
Defective instruments, disconnected high-temperature alarms and modifications made without risk analysis
Cost cutting, reduced maintenance and poor emergency preparedness

learnings.text: Safety barriers, technical and organisational, have to be kept working, particularly when a site is under financial pressure.
Modifications, including taking barriers out of service, need risk analysis and compensating measures.
Reduce hazardous inventory at source, control development around the site and tell neighbours how to protect themselves.

questions: Which of the unavailable barriers would you have treated as a condition for continuing to store MIC, and who should have had authority to enforce that?
How would an inherently safer design review treat the storage of a highly toxic reaction intermediate?

cases.name: Sandoz Schweizerhalle warehouse fire and Rhine pollution
cases.substance: agrochemicals including organophosphorus insecticides and mercury fungicides
cases.deaths_note: The sources read give no fatality figure.
cases.what_happened: A fire shortly after midnight destroyed a Sandoz chemical warehouse. Foam attack was overwhelmed and very large volumes of water were applied. Site drainage could not hold it, and most contaminated run-off entered the Rhine, killing aquatic life far downstream. The international Rhine alarm was delayed by nearly a day.
causes: Zurich City Police Science Department investigation: probably operator error with a blowtorch while shrink-wrapping sacks of Prussian blue (as reported by LPB 251)
Smouldering could go unseen for hours before rapid open fire
Site drainage could not cope with firefighting water

learnings.text: Provide tertiary containment for firewater sized on realistic worst-case application rates.
Segregate hazardous substances into suitably sized compartments and make sure workers and fire services understand the bulk storage fire risk.
Plan fire strategy in advance by scenario, comparing options including controlled burn-down.

questions: For your largest warehouse, where would the firewater go after the first hour?
Under what pre-agreed conditions would you let a warehouse burn rather than extinguish it?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: Eawag states the disaster led directly to Switzerland's Major Accidents Ordinance; LPB 251 says the EU Seveso Directive was amended in 1988 to strengthen storage requirements.

cases.name: BP Grangemouth hydrocracker explosion
cases.deaths_note: IChemE's incident summary gives one fatality (a contract crane driver) and no other injuries. The HSE case page read does not state a toll.
cases.what_happened: While a hydrocracker was held on standby during recommissioning, high-pressure gas broke through from the high-pressure separator into the low-pressure separator when liquid level was lost. The low-pressure vessel, whose relief was sized only for fire, ruptured violently. Fragments travelled over 1 km and fire followed.
causes: Gas breakthrough from the high-pressure to the low-pressure separator
Low-low level trip disconnected or taken out of service years earlier, without management of change
Low-pressure separator relief not sized for gas breakthrough
Operators distrusted the main level reading and relied on a backup chart recorder, whose offset led them to believe the HP separator level was normal

learnings.text: Disconnect trips only after documented risk assessment and management of change confirm that alternative controls are adequate.
Review every high-pressure to low-pressure interface for adequate overpressure protection.
Relief sizing should state which scenarios were considered and rejected, so that a lost safeguard visibly reopens the case.

questions: For one HP/LP interface you know, what is the relief load on gas blow-by if the level trip fails?
How would your plant detect that a trip had been defeated for years?

cases.name: Shell Norco refinery catalytic cracker explosion
cases.deaths_note: Chemical Processing podcast says seven Shell workers were killed; a TapRooT blog says six employees. No official figure was read.
cases.what_happened: In the early hours a large release in the catalytic cracking unit ignited and exploded, killing workers, damaging homes in the surrounding community and leading to evacuation. The blast was reported to have been felt far beyond the refinery.
causes: Trade-press account: believed catastrophic failure of a corroded vapour line off a depropanizer overhead
TapRooT blog: no definite cause was found
No official investigation report was read

learnings.text: The podcast guest stresses corrosion management that understands process chemistry and targets inspection where damage is likely, such as elbows and welds.
The podcast guest stresses checking whether people still occupy old buildings near process units.

questions: How would you choose inspection locations on an overhead vapour line, and what local changes in process chemistry would move them?
Which occupied buildings at your site were never designed for blast, and who still works in them at night?

cases.name: Piper Alpha offshore platform disaster
cases.substance: gas condensate, crude oil and natural gas
cases.deaths_note: Cullen: 165 of the 226 persons on board plus two crew of a rescue craft, 167 in all.
cases.what_happened: A condensate leak in the gas compression module ignited. Oil fires followed and the control room and main power were lost. Fire then ruptured gas pipeline risers connected to other platforms, massively intensifying it. Smoke and flame prevented evacuation from the accommodation by helicopter or lifeboat.
causes: Night shift tried to restart a condensate pump unaware that its relief valve had been removed; the blank flange fitted was not leak-tight
Failures of shift handover communication and the permit to work system

Riser failures massively fed the fire. The fire-water system was disabled by damage or power loss; the diesel fire pumps had also been left on manual, so even if undamaged they would not have started without manual action
Superficial management attitude to major hazard risk and weak emergency training

learnings.text: Require a formal safety assessment of major hazards, presented to the regulator as a safety case.
Provide a temporary safe refuge with defined endurance, with escape routes and embarkation assessed.
Prevent equipment still under maintenance from being returned to service, through an effective permit system and shift handover.

questions: How would a night-shift operator on your plant learn that a relief valve on a standby pump had been removed?
What hazards can reach your facility through pipelines connected to sites you do not control?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: A key Cullen recommendation was put into effect in 1992 through the UK Offshore Installations (Safety Case) Regulations. The industry account says industry accepted all 106 recommendations.

cases.name: Ufa (Asha) NGL pipeline and passenger train disaster
cases.substance: natural gas liquids (reported as propane and butane)
cases.deaths_note: Both sources read give 575; no official investigation report was read. They differ on prosecutions: Moscow Times says nine officials were charged; RailTarget says nine were charged and seven served sentences.
cases.what_happened: A liquids pipeline leaked about a kilometre from the Trans-Siberian railway and a flammable cloud collected along the track in the night. When two passenger trains passed through the area, the cloud exploded, destroying carriages. Operators had reportedly seen pressure fall and restored it without checking for a leak.
causes: Leak from a pipeline near the railway; RailTarget reports a 1.7 m crack of unexplained origin
Pressure drop answered by restoring pressure instead of searching for a leak
Gas accumulated near the track in the prevailing weather; reported smell not acted on
Ignition disputed: Moscow Times says wheel sparks; RailTarget says the exact source is uncertain

learnings.text: An unexplained pressure drop on a hazardous liquid pipeline should trigger leak confirmation or shutdown before throughput is restored.
Where pipelines run near transport corridors, there needs to be a direct way to stop traffic when a leak is suspected or reported.

questions: What evidence should a controller require before restoring pressure after an unexplained drop?
How would a public report of gas smell reach both your pipeline control room and the railway?

cases.name: Phillips 66 Houston Chemical Complex explosion
cases.what_happened: Contractors were clearing a blocked settling leg on a polyethylene loop reactor. The isolating ball valve above the open leg was open, and nearly the whole reactor inventory escaped within seconds. The vapour cloud ignited and exploded, followed by further explosions and fires.
causes: Single ball valve opened because its actuator air hoses were connected, and cross-connected
Practice relied on one valve instead of double block or blind flange required by company and industry practice
Permit-to-work not enforced
No fixed gas detection; control room and other occupied areas too close

Firewater came from the process water system, which was badly damaged; the fire pumps' power cables were attacked by fire, and of three standby diesel pumps one was under maintenance and another ran out of fuel

learnings.text: Study worst-case scenarios and escalation when setting layout, spacing and emergency plans.
Do not remove safeguards on live plant for any reason other than maintenance and testing.
An actuator whose hoses can be swapped defeats the intended fail position; design connections so they cannot be reversed.

questions: What isolation standard would you require before breaking containment on a reactor inventory, and how would you verify it in the field?
How would you design firewater so one explosion cannot disable it?

cases.name: Bright Sparklers fireworks factory explosion
cases.deaths_note: A 1993 DAP statement quoting the Royal Commission gives 22 dead and 103 injured; a 2020 New Straits Times feature gives 26 dead and 103 injured. The commission report itself was not read.
cases.what_happened: A factory chemist was testing a new product at a fireworks factory next to a village. Chemicals from the experiment spilled and started a fire that reached stored large firecrackers, causing a series of explosions that damaged nearby homes.
causes: Spill during product testing started a fire that spread to stored fireworks
Royal Commission (as quoted): the company broke many laws in a dangerous operation
Royal Commission, as quoted in a DAP statement: certain government departments did not properly perform statutory duties on the factory's siting, construction, maintenance and operation

learnings.text: The Royal Commission, as quoted, linked the long-undetected illegal operation to certain government departments not properly performing their statutory duties.
Where several agencies regulate one site, their enforcement should be coordinated.
Experimental work with energetic materials must be separated from stored product, and explosive sites need separation from housing.

questions: How would you set separation distances between testing, storage and housing at a pyrotechnics site?
When several agencies each regulate part of a site, how do gaps get found?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The New Straits Times reports that the fire service's hazardous materials unit was established after the disaster.

cases.name: Guadalajara sewer explosions
cases.deaths_note: Disputed. A 2022 journal article, citing earlier researchers, gives official figures of 210 dead and 2 missing, with unofficial estimates of 252 to 700 dead. Expansion (news) gives 206. Petitioners to the Inter-American Commission listed 224 fatalities which they said were based on official figures.
cases.what_happened: A series of explosions in the underground sewer system tore up kilometres of streets in a densely populated district. Residents had reported strong gasoline smells from drains in the preceding days; officials and Pemex staff checked, but the area was not evacuated.
causes: Fuel in the sewers; petitioners and many others attributed it to a leak from a Pemex polyduct
The federal prosecutor's version: several factors, including the Salamanca-Guadalajara polyduct rupture, urban train works and an improperly mounted water pipe on the polyduct
Defence experts held that the polyduct leak came after the explosions

Criminal case against accused officials, including Pemex employees, dismissed without convictions; Expansion reports that the federal prosecutor's investigation cleared Pemex, which was never criminally charged

learnings.text: Fuel smells in drains were reported for days without an evacuation decision, and state and municipal authorities later blamed each other for no order being given; evacuation authority should be settled in advance.
Give one named role the authority and a gas-reading trigger to evacuate when flammable vapour is found in a public drain.
Check crossings and contacts between pipelines and other buried services during design and third-party construction.

cases.name: Hickson & Welch jet fire
cases.what_happened: A still base was opened for cleaning for the first time in about 30 years. The residue was warmed with steam and raked out by hand. It decomposed and ignited, sending a jet fire through the manway into a nearby control building and on to the office block. Five people died.
causes: Residue and vessel atmosphere not analysed; sludge wrongly assumed thermally stable
Temperature probe sat above the sludge and a faulty steam regulator supplied hotter steam than intended
No permit for the raking task and inlet not isolated; metal rake used
Occupied buildings close to the plant; weak management of organisational change

learnings.text: Assess organisational change carefully, including workload and training.
Consider siting and structure of control rooms and occupied buildings near process plant, with doors opening outwards.
Practise muster and roll-call procedures routinely.
First-time cleaning of long-accumulated residue should be treated as a new process needing sampling and reactivity review.

questions: What would your permit system require before heating an unknown residue?
Does your temperature instrument measure the material that can run away, at all inventory levels?

cases.name: Texaco refinery (Pembroke Cracking Company) explosion

cases.what_happened: An electrical storm and a lightning-started crude unit fire upset the refinery. About five hours later, liquid pumped into a vessel whose outlet was shut overflowed through the relief system to the flare. The FCC flare knock-out drum outlet line failed, releasing about 20 t of hydrocarbons that exploded.
causes: Level control valve shut while the control system showed it open
Rupture of a corroded flare knock-out drum outlet elbow under liquid carry-over
Earlier modification had reduced the drum's liquid pump-out capability without adequate assessment
Alarm flood and poor control displays; unit kept running when it should have been shut down

learnings.text: Prioritise safety-critical alarms, document responses and limit total alarm numbers to what an operator can handle.
Give control displays process overviews, including mass and heat balance information.
Subject all modifications, including emergency ones, to formal hazard analysis.
Provide flare knock-out drums with critical high-level alarms and enough liquid removal capacity to prevent carry-over.

questions: How would your operators detect a mass-balance error when a valve position indication is false?
What conditions should force shutdown of a unit during a site-wide upset?

cases.name: Esso Longford gas plant explosion
cases.substance: hydrocarbon gas, condensate and oil (lean oil absorption plant)
cases.what_happened: Loss of lean oil flow let a reboiler heat exchanger in Gas Plant 1 chill far below its normal temperature. When warm oil was reintroduced the cold vessel suffered brittle fracture. Released hydrocarbons ignited; two employees died and Victoria's gas supply was cut.
causes: Lean oil pumps tripped and were not restarted for hours while cold fluids kept flowing through exchanger GP905
Reintroducing warm lean oil into the embrittled exchanger caused brittle fracture
Operators and supervisors did not know the hazard: inadequate training and no current procedures
Planned HAZOP of Gas Plant 1 never took place

learnings.text: A planned retrospective HAZOP, had it been done, would have exposed the loss-of-lean-oil cold hazard and led to procedures and training.
An unreported earlier cold temperature incident was a lost chance to warn staff.

If the lean oil process is ever reinstated, protect equipment against low temperature with suitable steels or adequate warnings and shutdowns, and apply rigorous risk assessment. Separately, even without reinstatement, the Commission said emergency shutdown systems needed review to make sure the gas plants can be isolated from each other and from the CSP.

The Commission found that moving plant engineers off site was a permanent change that should have been risk assessed first and was not. It said the change may have contributed, but a direct causal link could not be established.

questions: Which deviations on a plant you know could take a vessel below its minimum design metal temperature, and how would an operator recognise it?
How would you assess the safety effect of moving plant engineering support off site?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The Royal Commission recommended that externally imposed, monitored obligations be placed on Esso through approval of a safety case or safety report.

cases.name: Jesse (Idjerhe) petroleum pipeline fire
cases.deaths_note: No official toll read. An AFP timeline on Al Jazeera gives 1,082 and dates the event 18 October; Nnimmo Bassey's article dates it 17 October and says over a thousand; its footnote cites a title giving 1,098.
cases.what_happened: Petrol escaped from a 16-inch NNPC products pipeline; accounts quoted in the source say it spread over farmland and into a river, drawing local people to it. It ignited, killing many, and burned for about five days.
causes: State company and military government alleged sabotage; the article says this was never substantiated
A retired army chief alleged a siphoning operation and deliberate ignition (unverified allegation)
Root cause described as still not established 22 years later

learnings.text: The author calls for replacing life-expired lines, regular integrity testing and transparent, immediate incident reporting and response.
A pipeline operator needs leak detection, fast shutdown and community warning in local languages whatever caused the breach.

Public blame before any investigation is no substitute for establishing the cause, and the author suggests that fear of prosecution led some families to take injured relatives out of hospital early, which may have added to the deaths.

questions: How quickly should a products pipeline operator detect and isolate a breach in a populated rural area, and how would you prove that capability?
What makes an incident investigation credible when the operator and government have an interest in the finding?

cases.name: Enschede fireworks warehouse explosions
cases.deaths_note: The ARIA sheet gives 22 deaths, including 4 rescuers (fire-fighters in its narrative), and also mentions 3 disappearances without explaining them further. Other published counts were seen only in search results and were not read.

It spread to storage containers and boxes, which exploded in sequence, ending in a very large blast. The surrounding neighbourhood was devastated and firefighters were among the dead.
causes: Initial cause of the workshop fire never determined
Stored quantities and hazard divisions did not match the authorisation, with most stock in a more severe hazard division than the one authorised
No separation between containers, unauthorised containers and inadequate fire protection
Weak inspection, enforcement and inter-agency communication (Oosting Commission, as summarised by ARIA)

Limited official inspection does not excuse an operator from regulatory duties.
Verify the declared explosive hazard division of imported goods before relying on it for layout, quantity limits or firefighting plans.

questions: How would responders on arrival know that the real hazard class was higher than licensed?
What separation and siting basis would you set for pyrotechnic storage near housing?

Initial investigation pointed to lack of inspection and maintenance of the line, which the refinery did not own
Unclear ownership is thought to have delayed isolating the line

cases.name: P-36 production platform explosions and sinking
cases.what_happened: An isolated-in-name drain tank inside a support column was pressurised by back-flow while the other drain tank was being emptied. It ruptured, broke a seawater pipe and released hydrocarbons. A second explosion killed emergency team members; the column flooded and the platform sank on 20 March.
causes: Operators lined up drain-tank water to the production header, against the operating manual
Starboard tank intake not positively isolated while its vent was blinded and pump removed; the atmospheric tank pressurised and burst
Tanks and seawater piping placed inside a stability-critical column
Open watertight manholes, dampers that failed to close and fail-set sea valve aided flooding
Alarm flood: 1,723 alarms in 17 minutes

learnings.text: Do not put process-connected tanks inside columns or pontoons where damage threatens stability.
Isolation procedures, permits and toolbox talks must cover every connection, including the inlet.
Run and update hazard studies, especially when converting a drilling unit to production.
Emergency teams need portable gas detectors, clear command instructions and drilled procedures.

questions: Draw the isolation you would require before removing the pump from an atmospheric drain tank. What protects it from back-flow?
How should a conversion project re-check area classification and common-cause failures?

cases.name: AZF fertiliser plant ammonium nitrate explosion
cases.deaths_note: The ARIA sheet counts 31 people who died in the explosion or in the following days (our total): 21 on the AZF premises, 1 at the neighbouring SNPE works and 9 elsewhere.
cases.what_happened: Off-specification and rejected ammonium nitrate stored in a shed detonated on a weekday morning at a fertiliser works near the city. Court-appointed experts (2006) attributed it to sodium dichloroisocyanurate (named dichlorocyanurate in the sheet) meeting ammonium nitrate shortly before the blast

learnings.text: Do not exclude severe scenarios from hazard studies and emergency plans only because experience suggests they are very unlikely.
Reduce hazard potential at source, and control urban development around existing hazardous sites.
Waste and off-specification streams need the same compatibility controls as product, or tighter ones.

Which scenario has your hazard study screened out on historical grounds, and what if that judgement is wrong?

cases.name: Idemitsu Hokkaido refinery tank fires after the Tokachi-oki earthquake
cases.substance: naphtha (full-surface fire); the product in the ring-fire tank is not stated in the sources read
cases.deaths_note: The sources read do not state a death toll for the refinery fires.
cases.what_happened: Long-period ground motion caused large sloshing in floating-roof tanks. A ring fire broke out on one tank, and several floating roofs sank. About two days later the exposed naphtha in a tank with a sunken roof ignited despite foam application and burned as a full-surface fire for 44 hours.
causes: Large sloshing from 4-8 s ground motion in a deep sedimentary basin, above the code assumption
Ring fire: sparks from roof collision with gauge pole and guide supports
Naphtha fire: roof sank; inferred static sparks from isolated foam on the exposed liquid

learnings.text: Seismic design for tanks should use site- and period-specific long-period spectra and check sloshing, including higher modes.
Preventing floating roofs from sinking is important to prevent fire; check roof and pontoon strength.
Lower operating levels reduce the likelihood of fire and spill.

questions: How would you set maximum fill height for a floating-roof tank in a long-period seismic zone?
What are the ignition risks of foaming an exposed light-hydrocarbon surface, and how would you manage them?

Keep the public and non-essential people out until the scene is confirmed safe.
Wagon securing and train marshalling are process safety controls when oxidisers and fuels travel together.

Undersized atmospheric blowdown drum and stack instead of a flare
Occupied temporary trailers sited close to the stack
Fatigue, staffing, training, handover and procedure failures in startup
Senior management weak on major-hazard safety culture; budget cuts

Evaluate vessel overfilling in relief design and replace atmospheric blowdown with safer disposal such as flares.
Give distillation towers effective level instruments and automatic controls, and displays showing material balance.
Use leading and lagging process safety indicators, and address fatigue.

cases.name: Buncefield oil depot overfill, explosion and fire
cases.deaths_note: MIIB: 43 injured, none seriously, and no fatalities.
cases.what_happened: A petrol tank being filled by pipeline overflowed overnight after its level gauge stopped changing and automatic shutdown did not occur. Fuel cascading down the tank formed a large vapour cloud that spread off site. Explosions followed around 06:00, then a fire engulfing more than 20 large tanks.
causes: Tank 912 level reading stayed static from about 03:00 while filling continued
The independent high-level protection that should have closed valves did not operate
Overflowing petrol cascading from the tank top created a rich vapour cloud

learnings.text: Fit a high-integrity automatic overfill prevention system physically and electrically independent of the tank gauging system.
Set the integrity of overfill protection by systematic safety integrity level assessment following BS EN 61511 principles, with periodic testing.
A level that stays flat while a tank is receiving should itself raise an alarm.

questions: How would you prove that your independent high-level switch will work on the day it is needed?
Who can see, and who can stop, a transfer controlled from another organisation's control room?

cases.what_happened: Fire broke out shortly after midnight on a gas pipeline where maintenance work for new tie-ins was under way. Most of the dead worked for the contractor doing the work.
causes: Occurred during maintenance work for new tie-ins
An unnamed industry source said workers were welding a plate on the pipeline
Aramco set up a technical committee; its findings were not read

learnings.text: Tie-ins and hot work on or beside live gas lines need verified isolation or an engineered hot-tap procedure, with minimum people in the hazard area.
Contractor crews should be inside the same permit, gas testing and emergency escape arrangements as the operator.

cases.name: T2 Laboratories runaway reaction
cases.what_happened: During the first reaction step of an MCMT batch, the operator reported a cooling problem. Minutes later the reactor burst and its contents ignited. Employees were killed, people at neighbouring businesses were injured, and debris travelled up to a mile.
causes: Root cause: the company did not recognise the runaway hazard of the process
Cooling system open to single-point failure (likely loss of cooling started the runaway)
Reactor relief system could not relieve a runaway

learnings.text: CSB recommended adding reactive hazard awareness to undergraduate chemical engineering curricula.
Characterise heat of reaction and secondary decomposition before scale-up, and size cooling and relief from those data.

A long production record does not show that a process is safe. T2 was on its 175th batch, and CSB records unexpected exotherms in three of the first ten; investigate such excursions instead of relying on later successful batches.

questions: What calorimetry would you require before approving this kind of batch step at full scale?
With loss of cooling, how much time is there, and what independent action would use it?

cases.name: Imperial Sugar dust explosions
cases.what_happened: A first sugar dust explosion occurred in a recently enclosed belt conveyor under storage silos. It lofted dust built up on floors and high surfaces, causing secondary explosions through the packing buildings and nearby areas. Blast damage blocked exit routes and fires destroyed buildings.
causes: Conveying equipment not designed or maintained to limit dust release
Poor housekeeping let large dust deposits build up
Newly enclosed conveyor allowed explosible concentration; overheated bearing was the most likely ignition source
Inadequate emergency notification and no evacuation drills

learnings.text: Run a company-wide housekeeping programme to prevent hazardous dust build-up.
Design and operate to the combustible dust and electrical classification standards, and train workers and contractors.
Install an emergency alarm system and run evacuation drills.
Enclosing equipment changes the hazard and should go through management of change.

questions: What management-of-change questions should adding covers to a conveyor trigger?
How would you set and measure a dust accumulation limit that housekeeping can be audited against?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: CSB's report notes that after the incident OSHA announced it intended to start rulemaking on a combustible dust standard.

cases.name: Icepak coolstore explosion and fire, Tamahere
cases.what_happened: Firefighters attending a smoke detector alarm entered a coolstore plant room where they saw what appeared to be smoke, vapour or leaking refrigerant, apparently with no smell and no evident flammable-gas warning signs. A violent explosion followed, killing one firefighter, seriously injuring seven others and starting a large fire.
causes: Almost certainly a leak of flammable propane-based refrigerant ignited in the plant room, probably by electrical equipment
Fire Service did not know of the flammable refrigerant; no apparent warning signage or odorant
Plant room electrical equipment apparently not designed to be flame proof
Report notes systemic regulatory and information-sharing defects

learnings.text: Require odorant in large flammable gas installations and bring stationary refrigeration systems under hazardous substance controls.
Share hazardous substance information between agencies and use pre-incident planning to identify high-risk buildings, including outside urban districts.
Introducing a flammable refrigerant, even one marketed as a substitute for a non-flammable one, needs hazardous area, ventilation, detection and electrical review.

questions: What should a management-of-change review cover when a site that has used non-flammable refrigerants introduces a hydrocarbon blend?
What information and instruments should responders have before entering a plant room on an automatic alarm?

causes: External corrosion at the beach crossing
Ineffective anti-corrosion coating and cathodic protection there
Ineffective inspection and monitoring by the operator
Later inquiry: risk was foreseeable from the operator's own documents; regulatory arrangements were confused

learnings.text: Collate consultant, audit and safety case information; the inquiry found warnings were available to the operator but the risk was not addressed.
Regulatory competence and clear jurisdiction are essential to a safety case regime.
Parallel pipelines laid close together allow one rupture to escalate; spacing and isolation need explicit review.

What should a regulator do when an operator cannot produce integrity data for a critical pipeline?

cases.name: Sunrise Propane explosions
cases.deaths_note: The Fire Marshal release says two people died; it identifies a Sunrise employee found at the scene and a Toronto Fire district chief who died of a heart attack at the scene.
cases.what_happened: A series of explosions occurred at a propane facility in a Toronto neighbourhood. Thousands of people were temporarily evacuated. The Ontario Fire Marshal traced the start to a propane leak during a transfer directly between two cargo trucks.

Ignition source not determined

Siting of LPG facilities near homes should be judged on credible transfer-leak scenarios.

What would you require for siting a propane filling facility near housing?

cases.name: Viareggio LPG freight train derailment
cases.deaths_note: 32 fatalities from a 2014 peer-reviewed paper, which says the total includes two heart attack deaths and deaths up to six months later; the investigation body's annual report extract read does not state the toll.
cases.what_happened: A freight train of 14 LPG tank cars passed through Viareggio station at night when an axle on the first wagon failed. Cars derailed and the overturned lead car was punctured, releasing over 45 t of LPG. The dense cloud spread into neighbouring streets and ignited, with explosions, flash fire and pool fires.
causes: Italian rail investigation body: fatigue failure of a wagon axle due to lack of proper maintenance
Its annual report points to weak control and traceability of outsourced wagon maintenance
2014 paper: the tank was holed by a trackside object, with a stake or a switch assembly offered as hypotheses

learnings.text: Make basic maintenance rules for dangerous-goods wagons mandatory and keep safety-critical components traceable; certification alone was judged ineffective.
Consider removing or replacing trackside items that can cut or tear a derailed tank, starting at the most exposed urban sites.
A client's safety assurance cannot stop at checking that a maintenance contractor holds a certificate.

questions: What evidence beyond certification would you require from a firm maintaining safety-critical transport equipment?
Which fixed objects along a hazardous cargo route could puncture a derailed or overturned tank?

cases.name: Montara wellhead platform blowout
cases.deaths_note: The report states that the 69 personnel were safely evacuated.
cases.what_happened: A suspended well on the Montara wellhead platform kicked and flowed uncontrolled during return-to-well operations. All personnel were evacuated. Oil and gas flowed into the Timor Sea for more than ten weeks.
causes: Primary barrier, the cemented 9-5/8 inch casing shoe, failed; the cement job was compromised and not pressure tested
A second pressure-containing cap was never installed and the one fitted was later removed and not reinstated
No barrier complied with the company's own well construction standards at suspension
Systemic weaknesses in company competence, communication and records; weak regulatory oversight

learnings.text: Keep at least two tested and verified barriers in place whenever reasonably practicable, including batch operations.

Do not rely on a single barrier against blowout. The only exception should be a true emergency with the regulator's prior written approval, given only after a proper risk assessment, in exceptional circumstances and with risk reduced as low as reasonably practicable.
Anomalies in a barrier installation must trigger testing and remediation; a plan on paper does not prove a barrier exists.

questions: What test results would you require before counting a cement shoe as a well barrier?
How should day/night, rig/shore and contractor handovers record the status of safety-critical barriers?

cases.name: Indian Oil Jaipur POL terminal vapour cloud explosion
cases.deaths_note: The inquiry report gives 11 (six from IOC, five outsiders).
cases.what_happened: While petrol was being lined up for transfer, a large leak came from a Hammer Blind valve. The operating crew were overcome or absent, and the leak ran uncontrolled for about 75 minutes. The vapour cloud then exploded and the fire spread to all tanks, burning for about 11 days and destroying the terminal.
causes: Normal valve operating sequence not followed during line-up
Hammer Blind valve design left a large opening during changeover
No site-specific written procedure and no usable remote shut-off
Poor understanding of the hazard; emergency shutdown backup and control-room cover lacking

learnings.text: Provide remote isolation and design changes that make operator error less likely.
Site large installations using quantitative risk assessment and consider buffer-zone land-use controls.
Have site-specific written procedures and keep redundant safety systems in working order.
A long uncontrolled loss of containment must be treated as a credible event in hazard identification.

questions: How would you design the tank outlet line-up so that no single sequence error can open the tank to atmosphere?
What detection and response should work if the only operators present are incapacitated in the first minute?

cases.name: Macondo blowout, Deepwater Horizon
cases.place: Macondo well, Gulf of Mexico off Louisiana
cases.what_happened: During temporary well abandonment, a failed bottom cement barrier was wrongly judged sealed after a pressure test. Mud was removed and hydrocarbons flowed undetected for almost an hour. Gas reached the rig and ignited. The blowout preventer did not seal the well; the rig sank.
causes: Cement barrier not effectively installed; negative pressure test misread
Influx not detected in time
Blowout preventer had latent faults (miswiring) and buckled drillpipe stopped the blind shear ram sealing
Operator and contractor had vague safety roles; process safety got less attention than personal safety

learnings.text: Treat people as safety barriers and design and manage them with their limits in mind.
Close the gap between work as planned and work as done in safety-critical well operations.
Test and verify safety-critical elements, including redundant emergency systems, for latent failure.
Measure process safety indicators with the same effort as personal injury statistics.

questions: What acceptance criteria and independent check would you set for a negative pressure test?
How can a redundant emergency system be proof-tested so that one dead channel cannot hide?

cases.name: Cosmo Oil Chiba refinery LPG sphere fire and BLEVEs
cases.deaths_note: The IChemE summary lists 0 fatalities and 6 injuries.
cases.what_happened: The Tohoku earthquake damaged the leg braces of an LPG sphere that was full of water for inspection. In an aftershock it collapsed and broke adjacent LPG pipes. A locked-open emergency block valve kept feeding the fire, and successive BLEVEs destroyed the LPG tank farm and affected neighbouring plants.
causes: Water-filled sphere carried much more weight than the LPG design case; braces and legs failed
Water left in for 12 days instead of the usual 2-3
Emergency block valve locked open, against regulations
Pipe damage on collapse, tight spacing and delayed firefighting escalated the event

learnings.text: Strengthen sphere legs and braces in seismic areas, including for water-filled conditions.
Include natural-hazard triggers in emergency planning and drill with degraded access and communications.
Provide piping flexibility near spheres so a collapse is less likely to break lines.
A defeated emergency isolation valve needs formal approval, time limits and compensating measures.

questions: Which temporary conditions, such as hydrotest water, should be design load cases combined with earthquake?
How would your bypass register have treated the locked-open valve?

cases.name: Mitsui Chemicals Iwakuni-Ohtake resorcinol plant explosion
cases.deaths_note: The committee report gives 1 dead and 25 injured.
cases.what_happened: A steam failure led to emergency shutdown of a batch oxidation reactor. About an hour later an operator released the interlock to speed cooling, which also stopped the nitrogen that kept the liquid mixed. Peroxide in the uncooled upper section decomposed, and the reactor burst, spreading fire to adjacent equipment.
causes: Interlock released, stopping nitrogen and agitation
No cooling coil in the upper liquid and thermometer for the interlock only in the lower part
No criteria in the manual for releasing the interlock; release was easy and its side effect undocumented
No alarm for loss of agitation gas; the main control screen did not show nitrogen flow and made the temperature distribution hard to read once agitation stopped
Underlying: weak risk assessment, loss of skills and disregard of rules

learnings.text: Make the reactor inherently safer after emergency shutdown with both hardware and procedural measures: cool it promptly, keep it agitated, and define clear stable conditions under which the interlock may safely be released.
Address underlying causes: risk assessment, passing on skills, rule compliance and ownership of hazards.
A safe state after trip should be defined in measurable terms, and resetting a trip must not silently remove a protective function.

questions: How would you redesign the interlock so that changing cooling mode cannot stop mixing?
Where should temperature sensors be if agitation can fail?

A company officer suggested toluene might have ignited after excessive heat; no final investigation was read

Community warning arrangements around petrochemical estates should be tested.

What non-flammable or lower-hazard cleaning options would you evaluate first?

cases.name: Amuay refinery vapour cloud explosion
cases.deaths_note: COENER report gives 42 dead and 5 missing as the official figures and cites unofficial estimates of more than 95 dead. No official final report was read directly.
cases.what_happened: A cloud of flammable gas in the Block 23 storage area of the refinery ignited at about 01:10, causing a vapour cloud explosion followed by tank fires. Plant installations and nearby shops, schools and homes were destroyed.
causes: State investigation (as reported in news): deliberate sabotage, with intentionally loosened bolts on a gas pump
Non-official COENER report: most probably mechanical seal failure on one or more P-200 olefin pumps
COENER: gas present for hours without alarm activation or evacuation

COENER (non-official): weak maintenance and safety culture. A news report says an opposition investigation blamed poor maintenance and underinvestment; the files read do not show whether that was a separate study

COENER recommends respecting safety zones around refineries and independent audits of sites near communities.
When official and independent accounts conflict, teach both and ask what physical evidence would separate them.

questions: What evidence would distinguish seal failure from tampering on a pump flange or gland?
With a confirmed uncontrolled light-hydrocarbon leak, what triggers alarm and off-site evacuation?

AP reported executives saying a valve apparently failed during routine testing
No official investigation report was read

Early company statements are not a root cause; look for the final investigation before drawing technical lessons.

cases.name: Gumi hydrogen fluoride release
cases.place: Gumi National Industrial Complex, North Gyeongsang
cases.what_happened: While anhydrous hydrogen fluoride was being moved from a tank lorry to dilution equipment, a valve was opened by mistake and several tonnes escaped. Five workers died, thousands of people later sought medical attention, and responders were among those exposed.
causes: Worker error opened a valve during transfer for dilution

The tank lorry was pressurised for the transfer and release continued until the pressurising pump was switched off after about 30 minutes. The modelling paper says full closure of the lorry valve took about 8 hours, but judges that little escaped after the pump stopped.

learnings.text: Toxic transfer connections need remote emergency isolation and design that prevents unintended valve opening.
Responders need chemical-specific protective equipment and guidance for HF before an event; a study of responders linked symptoms to proximity, duration and lack of respiratory protection.

cases.name: Nippon Shokubai Himeji acrylic acid tank explosion
cases.deaths_note: One municipal firefighter died; ARIA counts 37 casualties in total including this death.
cases.what_happened: An intermediate tank was filled during a column test without its upper recirculation running. Uncooled upper layers dimerised and then polymerised. White vapour revealed the runaway; water spray on the insulated tank did not help. The tank burst while firefighters were nearby, and the contents ignited.
causes: Upper recirculation not started, leaving liquid above the cooling coil stagnant and uncooled
No temperature instrumentation on the tank
Outdated manual and poor training for an infrequent operating mode
Weak oversight of modifications (a cooling loop designed for 25 m3 was not upgraded) and of maintenance (removal of the steam-trace temperature control was not logged)
Earlier polymerisation incident not shared; late call to the fire service

learnings.text: Review risk and barriers for even minor changes and update operating documents to match.
Train for infrequent operating phases.
Continuously monitor parameters critical to runaway for each reactive material.

questions: Which hazard study prompt would have caught that cooling capacity only covered part of the tank volume?
When should firefighters withdraw from a vessel with a suspected runaway, and who tells them?

cases.name: West Fertilizer fire and explosion
cases.deaths_note: CSB final report: 12 emergency responders and 3 members of the public (15). The CSB web page summary says twelve volunteer firefighters and two members of the public, while its video description says 15 fatalities.
cases.what_happened: A fire at a fertiliser storage and retail site led, about 20 minutes after the first emergency calls, to detonation of ammonium nitrate. Responders and residents were killed, many were injured, and homes, schools and a nursing home nearby were badly damaged.
causes: CSB: combustible building and bin materials and combustibles stored nearby fed the fire and likely led to detonation
CSB: no fire detection or sprinklers; no pre-incident planning or FGAN response training
CSB: the town had grown up close to the site
Fire origin: CSB (January 2016) reported no final determination; in May 2016 ATF ruled the fire intentionally set (read via news report)

learnings.text: Keep combustibles away from ammonium nitrate and use noncombustible buildings and bins, and also provide fire detection and automatic sprinklers. CSB addressed recommendations on these points to code and regulatory bodies.
Fire services need pre-incident planning and specific ammonium nitrate hazard training.

CSB found shortcomings in regulation, land-use planning and insurer oversight. Its recommendations addressed regulatory coverage and insurer guidance, among other things; none of its numbered recommendations was a land-use planning measure.

questions: When should a fire service withdraw rather than fight a fire near ammonium nitrate, and what information would it need in advance?
How should planners treat a rural store that housing and schools have since surrounded?

cases.name: Lac-Megantic runaway oil train
cases.what_happened: A parked, unattended 72-tank-car crude train on a grade lost locomotive air-brake pressure after its engine was shut down following a fire. With too few hand brakes, it rolled about seven miles and derailed in the town centre in the early hours (it was parked on the evening of 5 July). Fire and explosions followed.
causes: Too few hand brakes; the effectiveness test was done with locomotive air brakes still applied
Shutting down the locomotives let air leak away from the independent brakes
A poor earlier engine repair led to the locomotive fire
Weak company safety culture, training and supervision; weak regulatory follow-up and SMS audit

Tank cars met the requirements then in force but were of an older standard; almost every derailed car was breached, and enhanced safety features could have reduced the damage. Separately, the crude was more volatile than shipping documents described, which the TSB treats as a risk

learnings.text: Railways need additional physical defences against runaway trains.
The regulator should check that safety management systems work, not only that they exist.
Flammable-liquid tank cars need tougher protection standards, and routes for dangerous goods should be risk-planned.

questions: Design a securement test that cannot be passed with the air brakes still holding the train. What independent barrier would you add?
How should information about changes in equipment state, such as a locomotive being shut down, reach someone competent to judge the brake effect?

Oil collected and vaporised in a confined conduit
Slow reporting and poor emergency assessment
Sparks from a non-explosion-proof hydraulic hammer without effective gas testing

Report leaks immediately and set isolation areas based on fire and explosion risk.
Account for urban growth around old pipelines and keep separation from buildings.

cases.what_happened: Condensate and gas leaking from a corroded pipeline, probably since the previous night, formed a vapour cloud. It ignited early in the morning, possibly from a stove being lit at a tea vendor's. The fire engulfed nearby dwellings and tea stalls.
causes: Line designed for dry gas carried wet gas with water and condensate, causing internal corrosion
Committed gas dehydration units were not installed
Inquiry committee: GAIL's systems or approach to repeated repairs of the high-pressure lines appeared inadequate and was a factor; it found individual culpability hard to establish

Inspect lines thoroughly, provide leak detection and patrol the route.

cases.name: Kaohsiung underground propylene pipeline explosions
cases.what_happened: A buried propylene line leaked into a storm drain trench. Operators saw abnormal pressure and flow, ran a static pressure test and restarted pumping. Gas spread more than 4.5 km while responders could not identify it, then ignited about three hours after the leak, blowing up roads under crowded streets.
causes: Pipe exposed to humid air inside a drain trench corroded from 6 mm to under 1 mm

The abnormal flow and pressure led to a stop and a static test, but pumping was restarted and a remaining flow discrepancy was left for later; neither company told the fire bureau or other authorities
At least 90,000 kg estimated released into a connected trench network
Probable ignition by a fire truck above a cable junction box (authors' analysis)

learnings.text: Include leaks into underground trenches in pipeline risk assessment and keep accurate pipeline and drain plans for responders.
Control ignition sources strictly; dispersal to below the flammable limit is the only safe outcome of such a leak.
Do not restart a line after an unexplained pressure or flow anomaly until the discrepancy is resolved by a test capable of finding the leak.

questions: Why could a static test at vapour pressure fail to reveal a leak in a liquefied gas line, and what test would you require?
How should an incident commander set the exclusion zone when gas may be travelling in drains?

cases.name: Kunshan Zhongrong aluminium dust explosion
cases.deaths_note: 75 died immediately; the toll later rose to 146 (AP, December 2014). Early reports give 75.
cases.what_happened: A dust explosion hit a factory that polished aluminium vehicle wheels. Many injured workers later died in hospital.
causes: Preliminary finding: a flame in a dust-filled room
Inadequate ventilation and dust removal and a substandard electrical system
Rules on dust cleanup, explosion-protected equipment, building spacing and line density ignored
Earlier dust warnings ignored and no safety training; weak local enforcement

learnings.text: Enforce dust cleanup, explosion-protected equipment, building spacing, production-line density rules and safety training.
Dust hazard analysis should cover metal-finishing shops, which may not be seen as process plants.

questions: How would you set housekeeping and dust-collector limits for an aluminium polishing shop?
How should production-line layout and the number of people exposed be treated as design variables that limit consequences?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The State Council dismissed the city's two top officials and others were put under judicial review (AP, December 2014).

cases.name: Accra flood and GOIL filling station fire
cases.deaths_note: A World Bank aide memoire on its 10-19 June 2015 mission attributes 150 deaths to the filling station fire, without giving an as-of date for that figure. Daily Graphic gives 159 for the flood and fire together.
cases.what_happened: During severe flooding, people sheltered at a filling station. Fuel mixed with the floodwater and ignited, burning people at and around the station.
causes: Flooding displaced fuel from the station; the government committee, as reported, cited leaking fuel tanks
Fuel floating on the water
Committee, as reported: a discarded lit cigarette ignited it

learnings.text: The government committee recommended drain dredging and training, certification and licensing of filling station attendants, among other measures.
Underground fuel storage design and siting must consider flooding: water ingress, tank displacement, vents and fill points below flood level.
Fuel on floodwater carries ignition hazard far beyond the station's classified zones.

questions: What flood scenarios should a filling station hazard study include, and what should staff do when water reaches the forecourt?
Should some flood-prone urban sites be closed to fuel retail, and by what criteria?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: A year later Daily Graphic reported that some filling stations had been demolished but that many committee recommendations had not been carried out.

cases.name: Tianjin port Ruihai warehouse explosions
cases.deaths_note: State Council investigators: 165 dead (including 99 firefighters and 11 police), plus 8 missing. The IChemE bulletin gives 173 including 104 firefighters.
cases.what_happened: A fire started in a container yard at a hazardous goods warehouse. Firefighters did not know what was stored. The fire spread to ammonium nitrate and two large explosions followed, the second much larger, devastating the surrounding area and dispersing other chemicals including sodium cyanide.
causes: Nitrocellulose dried out after loss of wetting agent, self-heated in hot weather and ignited
Fire spread to illegally stored ammonium nitrate
Containers stacked too close and quantities beyond permits; residences too near
Responders not told of the contents; company violations and failed official oversight

learnings.text: Keep self-reactive materials wetted and away from heat, and segregate them from oxidisers.
Emergency responders need reliable knowledge of stored materials and planning for hazardous chemical fires.
Coordinate regulation so that siting and permit limits are enforced.

questions: What inventory information should be available to the fire service within minutes, even at night?
How would you set separation and quantity limits in a mixed dangerous-goods yard?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The IChemE bulletin article reports that a national inspection of hazardous material storage sites followed.

cases.name: BASF Ludwigshafen North Harbour pipeline fire and explosion
cases.substance: butylene mixture (raffinate), ethylene and other pipeline products
cases.deaths_note: BASF's 2 December 2016 update gives four dead. Pipeline Technology Journal, reporting the court judgment, gives 5 dead (4 firefighters) and 44 injured.
cases.what_happened: During preventive replacement work on an emptied pipeline in a pipe trench, a cut was made into a neighbouring line that was not part of the job and held flammable raffinate. A fire started, and during early firefighting an explosion occurred, probably at an ethylene line, spreading fire along the trench.
causes: Prosecutor and police statement (translated by BASF): a line outside the work scope had been cut, apparently with a cutting disc
BASF preliminary view: leaking butylene mixture ignited by angle grinder sparks

Pipeline Technology Journal: a subcontractor accidentally cut the wrong pipe and was sentenced to one year on parole (it describes the work as welding); it also reports that BASF was mentioned as co-responsible during the trial but would not be prosecuted

learnings.text: Mark the exact pipe and cut location physically in the field and verify it jointly before any hot cutting in congested racks or trenches.
Emergency crews approaching a pipe-trench fire need to consider escalation from adjacent pressurised lines.

questions: How would you make it practically impossible to cut the wrong line in a crowded pipe trench?
What approach distance and information would your fire crew use at a pipe corridor fire?

cases.name: Ahmedpur East road tanker petrol fire
cases.deaths_note: 214 is the toll in the Dawn page read (July 2017), attributed to medical sources; it was still changing and a final official toll was not read.
cases.what_happened: A fuel tanker overturned on a highway. A large crowd gathered to collect the spilled petrol despite attempts by the driver and motorway police to clear the area. After about ten minutes the fuel ignited, engulfing the crowd.
causes: Regulator committee: tanker did not meet technical and legal standards for its load and carried a fake fitness certificate
Licensee remained responsible for outsourced haulage
Regulator report as quoted by Dawn: ignition attributed to low public awareness and to absent or late cordoning by local government and motorway police

Rollover cause not officially established: the article says the tanker overturned during a sharp turn, and also reports an unconfirmed account from police sources about driver fatigue. The ignition source had not been officially established

learnings.text: Hold marketers to a timed plan to bring contracted tankers up to safety rules.
Run public hazard awareness campaigns and review local patrol and quick-response plans.

questions: How should a fuel company assure the condition and certification of contracted vehicles?
What can the first two people at an overturned tanker realistically do about a gathering crowd?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The regulator OGRA fined Shell Pakistan Rs10 million and ordered compensation to victims.
