cases.name: Mongstad refinery cracker naphtha leak
cases.deaths_note: No deaths are reported; the report records no ignition and no symptoms in the operator who found the leak, but states no casualty count. This was a leak without fire.
cases.what_happened: An operator following up a report of an unusual smell found a naphtha leak from a small pump minimum-flow line in the cracker, caused by internal corrosion. The section was isolated and the plant evacuated. The leak did not ignite, but the investigators said ignition could have produced a substantial fire.
causes: Internal corrosion of a pump protection line
Changes in operating conditions, including salt handling by water washing and chemicals, not assessed for plant integrity
Inspection programme not revised after higher corrosion rates were found

Likely mechanism: ammonium chloride corrosion from inadequate chloride control, possibly linked to water washing or chemicals, with poorly controlled low flow causing deposits and condensation. Separately, the report found a weakness in information transfer: the night shift's smell observation was passed on only verbally (it did not cause the corrosion)

learnings.text: Review changes in operating conditions across disciplines for their effect on integrity and inspection.
Revise risk-based inspection when measured corrosion exceeds assumed rates.
Record safety-relevant observations at shift handover and assess exposure hazards, not only flammability, when clearing contaminated material.

questions: Which gradual changes in feed or washing practice on a unit would trigger your management-of-change process?
How should findings on one part of a corrosion loop change inspection of the rest?
cases.regulatory_aftermath: The Petroleum Safety Authority Norway identified four regulatory nonconformities and one improvement point.

cases.name: Tlahuelilpan pipeline explosion
cases.deaths_note: CENAPRED gives 137 deaths in total. A news report of 1 March 2019, citing the Hidalgo state government, gave 134.
cases.what_happened: An illegal tap ruptured a 14-inch gasoline line on the Tuxpan-Tula section. Soldiers found the leak in the afternoon; a large crowd gathered to collect fuel and did not leave when asked. Hours later the fuel exploded and burned.
causes: Illegal tap ruptured the pipeline
Large crowd gathered at the spill to collect gasoline
Military personnel were heavily outnumbered and could not clear the area
Ignition source not stated in the sources read

learnings.text: The CNDH made proposals to the authorities with prevention and non-repetition in view. Among them, Pemex should undergo an environmental impact assessment, including a risk study, for hydrocarbon transport even though not obliged to; the release also calls for affected people not to be stigmatised or criminalised and to have access to care.
A leaking liquid-fuel line in a populated or farmed area needs a pre-agreed plan covering shutdown of flow and crowd control.
Third-party interference belongs in pipeline hazard studies as a credible release cause with people present.

questions: On detecting a tap, what decides whether to stop pumping, and how fast can the line be isolated and the spill limited?
What can an operator do in advance when the public is likely to approach a release rather than flee it?

cases.name: Xiangshui Tianjiayi Chemical explosion
cases.what_happened: Nitrated waste that had been stored illegally for long periods at a chemical plant in an industrial park self-heated and ignited, leading to a massive explosion with heavy casualties both injured and dead, and large economic loss.
causes: Long-term illegal storage of nitrated hazardous waste
Heat accumulation took the waste past its autoignition temperature
Deficient safety management and safety awareness
Inadequate government supervision

learnings.text: Reactive wastes need the same thermal stability assessment, inventory limits and temperature monitoring as raw materials and products.
Inspections should reconcile waste generated against waste lawfully disposed of.

questions: How would you find undeclared or accumulating reactive waste on a site?
What data are needed to set a maximum pile size and residence time for a self-heating waste?

cases.name: Morogoro fuel tanker fire and explosion
cases.deaths_note: Toll rose as injured people died. Xinhua quoted a national hospital spokesperson giving 97 as of 19 August 2019 (not necessarily final); a 2022 burns-journal review says at least 89.
cases.what_happened: A fuel tanker overturned after an accident. People gathered to collect the leaking petrol, and the fuel ignited, causing a deadly fire and explosion.
causes: Tanker overturned and leaked
Crowd collecting spilled fuel around the wreck
Review attributes ignition to removal of the damaged truck's battery

learnings.text: Prevent the initial crash and, above all, deter people from collecting spilled fuel, which is linked to poverty.
A leaking tanker needs rapid cordoning and ignition control; responder arrival time and crowd control belong in transport risk assessment.

questions: How can a fuel distributor reduce harm in the first minutes after a rollover, before any emergency service arrives?
Which design, routing or social measures would you prioritise where spilled fuel has economic value to bystanders?

cases.name: LG Polymers styrene vapour release
cases.deaths_note: The High Power Committee gives 12 deaths in the immediate subsequent period and 585 hospitalised.
cases.what_happened: As the plant prepared to restart after a COVID-19 lockdown, styrene in a large storage tank polymerised and heated. In the early hours, vapour streamed from the tank vents into neighbouring settlements.
causes: Piping change inside the tank disrupted circulation, causing thermal stratification
Refrigeration run only in daytime; single bottom temperature sensor missed hot upper layers
Inhibitor monitored essentially only from bottom samples (top sampling very irregular); no inhibitor stock at the time and no dissolved oxygen monitoring
Rising polymer content treated as a quality issue, not a safety warning
No lockdown or restart procedure and no process safety management system

learnings.text: Treat idle or shutdown storage of reactive monomers as a separate operating mode with its own procedure and pre-startup safety review.
Measure temperature and inhibitor where hot spots can form, not at one convenient point.
In-tank piping changes need review of their effect on mixing and heat removal.
Quality data that indicate reaction progress should have safety alarm limits and an escalation route.

questions: Which measurements would give the earliest warning of runaway polymerisation in a 2,000-tonne tank, and what actions should each trigger?
How would your site decide what must keep running during an unplanned long shutdown?

cases.name: Baghjan-5 well blowout and fire
cases.deaths_note: The 2 are the Oil India firefighters reported killed in the June 2020 well fire (Deccan Herald). The expert committee volume read dates the explosion and fire to 9 June 2020; the news report of a ministry order dates the fire to 8 June. Later or other deaths were not checked.
cases.what_happened: During workover of a gas well, the blowout preventer was removed while a cement plug meant as the second barrier was untested. The well became live and blew out. It later caught fire, with damage to surrounding villages, wetland and wildlife.
causes: Cement plug placed far above the perforated zone and neither tagged nor pressure tested
BOP removed after 15 h of waiting on cement although the plan required 48 h
Hydrostatic head fell and the well became active; with the blowout preventer removed and no tested secondary barrier, it flowed and blew out
Deficient planning, execution discipline and supervision by contractor and operator (committee's stated probable reasons, preliminary)

learnings.text: Do not nipple down the BOP without a confirmed, tested secondary barrier; do not rely on fluid hydrostatic head alone.
Place the secondary barrier as close to the hydrocarbon zone as practicable.
Critical well operations need proper planning, adherence to procedure and on-site supervision.

questions: What hold points and sign-offs would stop BOP removal before barrier verification?
How should a client and a drilling contractor divide supervision of a critical workover step?

cases.name: Beirut port ammonium nitrate explosion
cases.deaths_note: No official figure was read. Human Rights Watch gives 218; the IChemE Loss Prevention Bulletin article gives 207.
cases.what_happened: A fire broke out in a port warehouse and several minutes later led to explosions, ending in a massive detonation of ammonium nitrate that had been held there for years after being taken off a detained ship. The port and much of the city were badly damaged.
causes: Technical-grade ammonium nitrate kept for years in an unsuitable port warehouse in a single stack
Fireworks and other combustibles stored in the same warehouse
Repeated written warnings did not lead to removal of the cargo
What started the fire is unresolved; welding is one debated theory

learnings.text: Ports should be developed and prepared to manage hazardous cargo that they are obliged to store but that is not part of their normal planned operations.
An oxidiser stock should be divided and segregated from fireworks, tyres and other fuels or ignition hazards.
A warning letter is not a control. Escalation routes need an authority that can act when the holder of the material cannot.

questions: Who in your organisation can force the removal of a hazardous inventory that is held under a legal dispute, and how long may that take?
How would you set separation, stack size and siting limits for an oxidiser store next to a populated area?

cases.name: Bata explosions at Nkuantoma military barracks
cases.substance: technical ammonium nitrate (explosives) and military ammunition
cases.deaths_note: 107 is the official-records figure quoted in the UN assessment.
cases.what_happened: A series of explosions hit the Nkuantoma gendarmerie and military barracks in a populated area. The UN assessment found the first and strongest blast was in a container area holding technical ammonium nitrate, which then set off the military arsenal and scattered unexploded ordnance across the city.
causes: First and strongest explosion in containers holding technical ammonium nitrate, which propagated to the ammunition depot
Local residents reported a fire may have started it; the assessment does not establish the initiating cause

learnings.text: Explosive materials and ammunition stores need separation distances so that one event cannot start the next.
Explosives storage next to housing turns a depot accident into a city disaster; siting must be reviewed as settlements grow.
Emergency plans for explosives sites must cover scattered unexploded ordnance and public access to debris.

questions: What separation and quantity limits would you require between two explosive stores, and how would you verify them over time?
How should a regulator oversee hazardous storage held by military or other bodies outside normal industrial permitting?

cases.name: BM Container Depot fire and explosions, Sitakunda
cases.deaths_note: The Business Standard gives 51; Prothom Alo's report on the port authority inquiry gives 49; bdnews24 says around 50. Firefighters were among the dead.
cases.what_happened: A fire at a private container depot holding hydrogen peroxide consignments among export cargo was followed by explosions while firefighters, who did not know of the chemical, applied water. The fire took days to put out and caused many deaths and injuries among workers, responders and others.
causes: Divisional Commissioner's committee attributes the fire/explosions to hydrogen peroxide and depot mismanagement
Port authority inquiry cites poor segregation, no hydrants and untrained staff and recommends probing possible sabotage
Other agencies said the depot lacked permission and other materials may have contributed
Peroxide containers delayed on site; packaging reported not to meet international standards

learnings.text: Segregate dangerous goods from other cargo, allow handling only at capable depots and require hydrants and coordination with fire stations.
Review the law and coordination between the many approving agencies for dangerous goods storage.
Depots need an on-site dangerous goods register that responders can read before choosing a firefighting method.

questions: What controls should apply when dangerous goods dwell far longer than planned at a logistics site?
How should a depot signal oxidiser hazards to arriving firefighters?

cases.name: Pertamina Plumpang fuel terminal fire
cases.substance: fuel (specific product not established in the sources read)
cases.deaths_note: Jakarta health agency figure as of 24 March 2023 (Jakarta Post). Early reports gave lower and changing counts (e.g. 17, 20, 23).
cases.what_happened: A fire started in the evening at the fuel terminal and spread into dense housing that lay very close to the boundary. Residents were killed and evacuation reports range from several hundred to thousands.
causes: No final investigation was read
Early statements: the police chief suggested a possible technical problem while a tank was being filled; Pertamina's chief said an inlet pipe burned and the tanks did not
Consequences linked to housing encroaching on the buffer area (a newspaper analysis puts the closest homes 28 m from the depot)

learnings.text: Establish and keep a buffer zone; a geography journal study recommends one extending 100 m from the depot's present outer wall (its abstract words this as a 50-100 m range).
A Parliament research brief calls for prevention to international standards, working detection and firefighting, and regular drills.
A buffer distance should come from consequence analysis and be protected by enforceable land-use control.

questions: Is it better to move an existing terminal, move its neighbours or reduce its hazard, and how would you compare them?
How would you check whether a fixed 100 m buffer is adequate for this terminal's credible scenarios?
